That changes it: VARCHAR(n) and TEXT use identical varlena storage in Postgres, so read performance is the same. The only difference is the length constraint on write.

The concrete cost of my answer: you'd choose a type based on false performance reasoning, when the real decision should be whether you want a length constraint enforced at write time (VARCHAR) or not (TEXT). For a description column, TEXT is usually the right choice because descriptions don't have a natural max length.
